summary: IDS feed s157_double is degraded: 8.4% of frames exceed IDS 1518B MTU and are dropped by NIC, plus 2.56 Gbps microbursts overload the 1 Gbps IDS port (256% capacity). Both cause silent packet loss and reduced detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding jumbo/encapsulated frames up to 8058 bytes without MTU normalization, while the IDS port/NIC is standard 1518B. 137 of 1634 frames (8.4% > 1% threshold) exceed the limit.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC drops oversized frames before analysis - 8.4% blind spot. IDS misses signatures, fails TCP reassembly and file extraction for those flows, and cannot detect attacks carried in large frames.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs_full_payload=true so broker slicing would break detection. Enable 9000B jumbo on IDS NIC/tool or configure broker to normalize MTU/slice only as last resort to prevent NIC-level drops.

findings.root_cause: Aggregate/burst rate from broker exceeds IDS port capacity. Peak 2.56 Gbps in 1ms burst vs 1 Gbps port (256% of capacity, threshold 80%) across 6 intervals - no load-balancing or shaping in front of IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS ingress buffers overflow and drops packets randomly during bursts. Causes missed detections, one-way flow artifacts, broken stream reassembly, and alert fatigue/false negatives under load.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2-3 IDS ports/instances via 5-tuple load balancing or add aggregation filtering to keep per-port utilization <80% and eliminate burst drops.
